label: Spatial overlap › Distribution
meaning: Characterises horizontal distribution of chondrichthyan species.

label: Encounter › Bathymetrical range
meaning: Vertical distribution of chondrichthyan species.

label: Encounter › Spatio-temporal distribution
meaning: Spatio-temporal horizontal and/or vertical distribution of chondrichthyan species (including seasonality, diel patterns, and other timings).

label: Capture › CPUE
meaning: Use of catch-per-unit-effort or related fishery-dependent catch metrics as an index of interaction or capture intensity.

label: Capture › Gear selectivity
meaning: Evidence that capture depends on gear design or configuration, determining which species or sizes are retained or excluded.

label: Capture › Catchability
meaning: Probability that a species is caught once exposed or encountered, driven by behaviour, morphology, sensory ecology, or gear interaction.

label: At-vessel mortality › AVM
meaning: Mortality occurring before release, during hauling, capture, handling, or time on deck or alongside the vessel.

label: Post-release mortality › Health assessment (physical)
meaning: Assessment of physical impairment at capture or release used as a proxy for subsequent survival.

label: Post-release mortality › Health assessment (behavioural)
meaning: Assessment of behavioural impairment at capture or release used as a proxy for subsequent survival.

label: Post-release mortality › Health assessment (physiological)
meaning: Assessment of physiological impairment at capture or release used as a proxy for subsequent survival.

label: Post-release mortality › PRM
meaning: Mortality occurring after release due to injury, physiological stress, predation risk, or delayed effects.

label: Area-based tools › Permanent Fisheries Restricted Areas
meaning: Permanent spatial closures or restricted areas intended to avoid bycatch by excluding fishing from high-risk areas.

label: Area-based tools › Temporal Fisheries Restricted Areas
meaning: Seasonal or temporary spatial closures applied during periods of elevated bycatch risk.

label: Area-based tools › Quasi-real time closures
meaning: Rapidly updated closures based on recent observations, forecasts, or risk indicators.

label: Area-based tools › Move-on rules
meaning: Rules requiring vessels to leave an area after a bycatch event or threshold is reached.

label: Area-based tools › Time-of-day restrictions
meaning: Restrictions on fishing at certain times of day or night to avoid periods of higher bycatch risk.

label: Area-based tools › Voluntary fleet communication
meaning: Fleet-led communication systems sharing bycatch hotspots or recent events to help vessels avoid risky areas.

label: Limiting effort › Vessel entry
meaning: Restrictions on the number or type of vessels allowed to participate in a fishery.

label: Limiting effort › Fishing capability
meaning: Limits on vessel size, engine power, hold capacity, or other attributes that determine fishing capacity.

label: Limiting effort › Fishing days
meaning: Limits on the number of days vessels are allowed to fish.

label: Limiting effort › Gear limits
meaning: Restrictions on the amount, size, or configuration of fishing gear that can be deployed.

label: Limiting effort › Soak duration
meaning: Limits on how long gear can remain in the water before retrieval.

label: Limiting effort › Number of fishing operations
meaning: Limits on the number of sets, hauls, or deployments over a defined period.

label: Limiting effort › Buyback programmes
meaning: Programmes that reduce overall effort by purchasing vessels, licenses, or gear out of the fishery.

label: Increase selectivity › Excluder grids
meaning: Grid devices or equivalent structures that allow non-target organisms to escape while retaining target catch.

label: Increase selectivity › Mesh size
meaning: Changes in mesh size to alter which species or size classes are retained or escape.

label: Increase selectivity › Hook size/type
meaning: Changes in hook design, size, or shape to reduce the capture of non-target species.

label: Increase selectivity › Weak hooks or breakable gear
meaning: Gear components designed to fail or release under the force of larger non-target species.

label: Increase selectivity › Hook shielding devices
meaning: Devices that physically shield hooks or bait to reduce unwanted hooking.

label: Sensory deterrents › Acoustic deterrents
meaning: Use of sound-emitting devices to deter or alert animals and reduce bycatch interactions.

label: Sensory deterrents › Magnetic deterrents
meaning: Use of magnets or electropositive materials intended to repel sensitive species such as sharks and rays.

label: Sensory deterrents › Electrical deterrents
meaning: Use of electric stimuli or electrified gear components to discourage interactions with fishing gear.

label: Sensory deterrents › Visual deterrents
meaning: Use of visual cues such as lights, colored materials, or conspicuous devices to reduce bycatch.

label: Sensory deterrents › Chemical deterrents
meaning: Use of chemical substances or scent-based deterrents to reduce attraction or contact with gear.

label: Reduce attraction › Bait modification
meaning: Changes in bait type, size, color, or presentation to lower attractiveness to bycatch species.

label: Reduce attraction › Artificial bait
meaning: Use of artificial or alternative bait types to reduce incidental attraction of vulnerable species.

label: Reduce attraction › Offal management
meaning: Measures controlling offal discharge or discard practices that may attract bycatch species during fishing.

label: Reduce attraction › Light or stimulus restrictions
meaning: Restrictions on lightsticks, lights, or other stimuli that can attract bycatch species.

label: Gear detectability › Gear detectability
meaning: Modifications that make gear more detectable to non-target species, improving avoidance, or modifications that reduce sensory cues that attract or expose gear to non-target species.

label: Reduce encounter › Fishing depth changes
meaning: Adjustments in fishing depth to reduce overlap with the vertical distribution of bycatch species.

label: Reduce encounter › Gear profile or configuration
meaning: Changes in gear profile, hanging ratio, height, or configuration that reduce contact with bycatch species.

label: Reduce encounter › Deployment timing
meaning: Adjustments in set or haul timing to avoid periods when bycatch species are more likely to encounter gear.

label: Reduce stress › Immediate release
meaning: Rapid release of live bycatch to reduce handling time and stress exposure.

label: Reduce stress › Improved handling
meaning: Handling protocols designed to minimize injury, stress, and physiological impairment.

label: Reduce stress › Improved deck condition
meaning: On-deck measures such as shade, water, ventilation, or soft surfaces that reduce stress while animals are aboard.

label: Reduce stress › Reduced air exposure
meaning: Measures specifically aimed at minimizing time exposed to air before release.

label: Reduce retention › Retention limits
meaning: Limits on the number or amount of bycatch individuals or species that may be retained.

label: Reduce retention › Retention ban
meaning: Rules prohibiting retention of specified bycatch species.

label: Reduce retention › Shark finning ban
meaning: Rules prohibiting finning or requiring sharks to be landed with fins naturally attached.

label: Reduce retention › Trade ban
meaning: Restrictions or bans on the sale or trade of species or products to discourage retention.

label: Reduce retention › CITES restrictions
terms: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
meaning: Trade controls linked to CITES listings that may reduce incentives to retain vulnerable species.

label: Offsets › Direct offsets
meaning: Compensatory conservation actions implemented directly by the entity responsible for residual bycatch impacts.

label: Offsets › Offset funding
meaning: Compensatory mitigation payments to a public or private body that implements offset conservation actions.

label: Offsets › Conservation banking
meaning: Use of biodiversity or conservation credits generated in advance to compensate residual bycatch impacts.

label: Distribution technology › Biologging
meaning: Animal-borne tags or sensors used to quantify movement, habitat use, and overlap relevant to bycatch.

label: Distribution technology › Environmental DNA
meaning: Use of eDNA to detect presence, habitat use, or distribution of species relevant to bycatch risk.

label: Fishing effort data sources › Vessel tracking
meaning: Automatic Identification System or Vessel Monitoring System vessel tracking data used to infer fishing effort and overlap with bycatch risk.

label: Gear-based sensing › On-gear cameras
meaning: Cameras attached to gear or deployed near gear to document interactions and bycatch behaviour.

label: Gear-based sensing › On-gear sensors
meaning: Sensors mounted on or integrated with fishing gear to detect gear behaviour, catch events, or potential bycatch interactions.

label: Gear-based sensing › AI species detection
meaning: Artificial intelligence systems used to detect, classify, or respond to bycatch species in near real time.

label: Decision-support systems › Dynamic risk forecasting
meaning: Systems that combine recent data and models to forecast bycatch risk and guide short-term decisions.

label: Decision-support systems › Onboard decision support
meaning: Tools that integrate monitoring, risk information, and regulations to support real-time skipper decisions.

label: Distribution methods › Species distribution models
meaning: Models estimating species distribution using non-fisheries data, such as surveys, telemetry, or environmental observations.

label: Distribution methods › Bycatch risk models
meaning: Models estimating spatial or spatio-temporal bycatch risk using fisheries-dependent data, alone or integrated with environmental predictors.

label: Risk assessment › Risk assessment frameworks
meaning: Frameworks evaluating vulnerability or risk of bycatch at species, population, or fishery level, including PSA, ByRA, and overlap-based risk metrics.

label: Management strategy evaluation › Management strategy evaluation
meaning: Simulation-based approaches used to evaluate alternative management scenarios, trade-offs, and expected bycatch outcomes.
